subject: CRAN notes: ggplot2 inside R packages

messages.author: 9d162dfa682d2d99
messages.subject: CRAN notes: ggplot2 inside R packages
parts:
Hi All, 

I am writing an R package for sensitivity analysis in phylogenetic methods: sensiPhy
My ploting functions use ggplot2 as standard. The problem is that CRAN tests gives many notes related to the global environment.
What is the best way to use ggplot2 functions inside new R packages to avoid these notes?

Thanks in advance,
Gustavo Paterno

See an example of the code and CRAN notes below:
ggplot2::ggplot(result,aes(x=slope,y=..density..),
                environment = environment())+
                geom_histogram(fill="lightyellow", alpha=.9,colour="grey60", size=.2) +
                geom_density(size=.2) +
                geom_vline(xintercept = slope.0,color="red",linetype=2,size=.7)+
                xlab("Estimated slopes")+
                theme(axis.text = element_text(size=14),

CRAN notes:
plot_influ_phylolm: no visible global function definition for ‘aes’
plot_influ_phylolm: no visible binding for global variable ‘slope’
plot_influ_phylolm: no visible binding for global variable
  ‘..density..’
plot_influ_phylolm: no visible global function definition for
  ‘geom_histogram’
plot_influ_phylolm: no visible global function definition for
  ‘geom_density’
plot_influ_phylolm: no visible global function definition for
  ‘geom_vline’
plot_influ_phylolm: no visible global function definition for ‘xlab’
plot_influ_phylolm: no visible global function definition for ‘theme’
plot_influ_phylolm: no visible global function definition for
  ‘element_text’

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: CRAN notes: ggplot2 inside R packages
parts: You need to either import those packages into your namespace or use ::

ggplot2::geom_density(size=.2) +
ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept =
slope.0,color="red",linetype=2,size=.7)+
ggplot2::xlab("Estimated slopes")+
ggplot2::theme(axis.text = element_text(size=14),

(I also doubt setting the environment to environment() is the right
thing to do, but it's hard to know without more context)

Hadley

parts:
Dear Hadley,

You are right, in general the problem was solved with the new ggplot2 version. 
However, I still have the problem when I need to extract variables names from a fomula and to use this variables inside aes mapping.
Please find attached/below a minimal reproducible example. 

outside a function, the plot works normaly:
library(ggplot2)
### Simulating data:
result <- data.frame(a = 1:100, b = 1:100 + rnorm(100,1,2))
formula <- log(a) ~ log(b)

### standard ggplot2:
#Extracting vars from formula:
vars  <- gsub("list","",attr(terms(formula),"variables"))[-1]
ggplot(result,aes(x= eval(parse(text=vars[2])),
                  y= eval(parse(text=vars[1]))))+
    geom_point(size=3,alpha=.8)+
    ylab(vars[1])+
    xlab(vars[2])

However, inside a function the code can not find the object 'vars':
### Removing vars from global envinronment:
rm(vars)
### using the same approach inside a function
test.fun <- function(data,formula) {
    vars  <- gsub("list","",attr(terms(formula),"variables"))[-1]
    p <- ggplot(result,aes(x=eval(parse(text=vars[2])),
                           y=eval(parse(text=vars[1]))))+
            geom_point(size=3,alpha=.8)+
            ylab(vars[1])+
            xlab(vars[2])
    print(p)
    
}

test.fun(data=result,formula = log(a) ~ log(b))

So it gives this error message:
Error in parse(text = vars[2]) : objeto 'vars' não encontrado

If I use the "solution" : environment <- environment () inside the function, then it works normaly again:
### with environment <- environment()
test.fun <- function(data,formula) {
    vars  <- gsub("list","",attr(terms(formula),"variables"))[-1]
    p <- ggplot(result,aes(x=eval(parse(text=vars[2])),
                           y=eval(parse(text=vars[1]))),
                environment = environment())+
        geom_point(size=3,alpha=.8)+
        ylab(vars[1])+
        xlab(vars[2])
    print(p)
    
}

test.fun(data=result,formula = log(a) ~ log(b))

So my question is if the "solution" 'environment <- environment()' is ok, specially inside a package.

Once again, thanks a lot for your support.

Best wishes,
Gustavo

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: CRAN notes: ggplot2 inside R packages
parts:
You need to read the section on aes_ and use that instead. I'd write
your function like this:

test_fun <- function(data, formula) {
stopifnot(inherits(formula, "formula"), length(formula) == 3)

mapping <- aes_(formula[[3]], formula[[2]])

ggplot(data, mapping, environment = parent.frame()) +
geom_point(size = 3, alpha = .8)
}

test_fun(mtcars, mpg ~ disp)



(If you're not using the dev version, I think you should be able to
use aes_q instead of aes_)

Hadley
